Robot models as rigid-body trees

Source: R/robot-model.R
robot_model.Rd

Builds a validated kinematic tree from links and joints. Every link except one root link has exactly one parent joint; the structure must be connected and acyclic. Closed kinematic chains are not representable and are rejected. The configuration vector q has one entry per movable (non-fixed) joint, ordered by a breadth-first traversal from the root that preserves the order joints were supplied in; see robot_joint_names(). The number of joints therefore can exceed the number of degrees of freedom when fixed joints are present.

Usage

robot_model(
  links = list(),
  joints,
  base = robot_pose(),
  end_effector = NULL,
  name = "robot"
)

Arguments

links

List of robot_link() objects. Links named by joints but missing here are created as massless links.

joints

List of robot_joint() objects.

base

Pose of the root link in the world frame.

end_effector

Name of the default end-effector frame. Defaults to the last leaf link in traversal order.

name

Model name.

Value

A robot_model object.

Examples

links <- list(robot_link("base"), robot_link("link1"), robot_link("link2"))
joints <- list(
  robot_joint("j1", "revolute", "base", "link1"),
  robot_joint("j2", "revolute", "link1", "link2", origin = transl(1, 0, 0))
)
robot <- robot_model(links, joints, name = "planar")
robot
#> <robot_model> planar: 3 links, 2 joints, 2 degrees of freedom
#> end effector: link2
#>  name     type parent child q_index lower upper
#>    j1 revolute   base link1       1  -Inf   Inf
#>    j2 revolute  link1 link2       2  -Inf   Inf
